newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to increase spring sowing area five pct.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to increase spring sowing area five pct.

text.p: Belarus plans to increase its spring grain sowing area by five percent this year, Agriculture Minister Vasily Leonov said on Wednesday.

Leonov, speaking during a live television and radio broadcast on the spring sowing campaign, said Belarus needed 25 percent more feedgrains, 50 percent more fodder and 40 percent more fertiliser, including 135,000 tonnes of nitrous fertiliser from Russia and Ukraine.

President Alexander Lukashenko, who chaired the broadcast, said that some nitrous fertiliser imports would be tax-free. "We will free them of part of the duties to support importers and producers of agricultural production," he said.
"Weather forecasters say spring will be long. It began early but will be accompanied by light frosts and negligible dampness in the earth," said Lukashenko, a former farm boss.
The former Soviet republic's spring sowing campaign, which usually starts in April, would last two weeks by order of the president, Leonov said, without giving further details on the start date.

Sowing began in two southern regions earlier this month when there was a thaw, and a senior ministry official said on March 12 that Belarus was predicting a net grain harvest of 6.5 million tonnes this year, above last year's 5.8 million.

The deputy head of the Agriculture Ministry's crop division, Vyacheslav Herasimovich, said the sowing area on collective farms and state farms had been increased to 2.6 million hectares from 2.58 million, bringing the total area, including private plots, to 2.70-2.75 million.
